title: Microsoft Teams: pin and organise resources in folders below the chat and channel header
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout schedule, automatic arrival, licensing context and absence of a documented feature switch agree with the sources checked. Two descriptive assurances go beyond the evidence: that the feature reaches no new data and that nothing acts autonomously; these should be narrowed to what Microsoft describes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Pinned resources are necessarily content already shared in the conversation, so the feature reaches no new data.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams pinned resources data; Teams pin file permissions header. Read roadmap, MC1473153, Graph pin-message reference and SharePoint/Teams integration excerpts; none restricts every new resource pin to previously shared content or establishes unchanged data access.
claims.fix: Replace the first Data exposure sentence with 'MC1473153 says existing resources from the removed panes remain accessible through the updated experience.' Replace the risk rationale with 'Low. MC1473153 describes a resource-management redesign, identifies no compliance considerations and asks for no admin action.'

claims.claim: Microsoft describes pinning resources and organising folders as actions users take.
claims.quote: Users will be able to pin frequently used resources directly below the chat or channel header, pin multiple messages alongside other resources, and organize them into folders.

claims.claim: Nothing in the feature acts on its own.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams pin folders automatically; Teams pinned resources data. Read roadmap, MC1473153 and Graph pin-message reference. They describe user pinning and organisation but do not establish the blanket absence of autonomous actions.
claims.fix: Replace the Autonomy & actions bullet with 'The roadmap and MC1473153 describe users pinning resources and organising them into folders; they describe no autonomous actions.'

claims.claim: No feature-specific prerequisites or administrative roles are stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams pin resources folders prerequisites admin roles sharing permissions. Read roadmap and MC1473153 in full, messaging policy documentation and returned Teams role excerpts; none specifies a prerequisite or configuring role for this redesign.
